sanskrit: sṛjāmy āpa uśatīr upemāḥ saṃrarāṇāḥ payasā saṃ babhūvuḥ | datto asmabhyaṃ draviṇeha bhadrā apāṃ prati prati gṛhṇātv enāḥ ||
english: I release these eager waters hither; mingling together, they have united with milk. The wealth given to us here is auspicious — may he who is lord of waters receive them back.

sanskrit: uc chrayasva bahur bhava svena mahasā yava | pṛṇīhi sarvā pātrāṇi mā tvā divyāśanir vadhīt ||
english: Rise up, grow large, O barley, by your own greatness. Fill all the vessels; may the heavenly lightning not strike you down.

sanskrit: āśṛṇvantaṃ yavaṃ devaṃ yatra tvācchāvadāmasi | tad uc chrayasva dyaur iva samudra ivaidhy akṣitaḥ ||
english: O divine barley who hears us, wherever we address you — rise up there, inexhaustible as the sky, grow as boundless as the ocean.

sanskrit: akṣitās ta upasado akṣitāḥ santu rāśayaḥ | pṛṇanto akṣitāḥ santv attāraḥ santv akṣitāḥ ||
english: Inexhaustible be your seed-stores, inexhaustible be your heaps. Those who fill the bowls shall be inexhaustible; those who eat shall be inexhaustible.

sanskrit: sakṛd yad dyaur ajāyata sakṛd bhūmir ajāyata | sakṛd yaḥ pṛśniyā dugdhaṃ tad anyo nānu jāyate mā tvānu jani kaś cana ||
english: Once the sky was born; once the earth was born; once the milk was drawn from the dappled cow — that which is unique is not born again. May no one be born after you.

sanskrit: iṣvagram iṣuyāvanaṃ maṇiṃ kṛṇve sumaṅgalam | sa mā śaravyābhyaḥ pātu divānaktaṃ ca jīvase ||
english: I make for myself the amulet that stands at the arrowhead and deflects arrows — the auspicious one. May it protect me from all missiles, by day and by night, that I may live.

sanskrit: pratiṣṭhito 'si brahmaṇā jambhayāmasi tvā vayam | apāmārgeṇa vidvalā idaṃ tvāpa mṛjmahe yuvantaṃ kṣipantaṃ jahi ||
english: You are established by sacred power; we, the knowing ones, crush you with apāmārga. With this we wipe you away — strike down the one who attacks the young, who hurls missiles.

sanskrit: śīrṇaṃ ta etan na kṣutaṃ ta etat saṃkṣutaṃ duḥkṣutaṃ tubhyam astu | rudrāśaniṣ ṭe jaghanena grīvā indra iva vṛtraṃ vajreṇa hantu ||
english: This sneeze of yours is broken, this sneeze is not auspicious — what is combined and ill-sneezed, let that ill-omen be yours. May Rudra's thunderbolt smite your hindquarters and neck, as Indra with the vajra smote Vṛtra.

sanskrit: anuhavaṃ parihavaṃ parivādaṃ parikṣavam | savyermaṃ riktakumbhāṃ parā tāṃ savitaḥ suva ||
english: The echo-curse, the surrounding curse, the circling slander, the circling sneeze — O Savitṛ, drive away that woman with the empty pot who walks on the left.

sanskrit: apapāpaṃ parikṣavaṃ puṇyaṃ bhakṣīmahi kṣavam | śivā te pāpanāsikāṃ parṇakaś cābhi mehatām ||
english: The ill-omened sneeze we drive away; may we partake of the auspicious sneeze. May the parṇaka plant urinate over the wicked-nosed one, and may it be propitious for you.

sanskrit: abhi tvā pañcaśākhena hastenādhāṃ sahīyasā | yathā na vidviṣāvahai na vibhavāva kadā cana ||
english: I have pressed you down with the five-branched, most powerful hand — so that we shall never hate each other, never quarrel at any time.

sanskrit: cākravākaṃ saṃvananam asyasya svaṃkaram | amuṃ svaṃ kṛṇotu me yam ahaṃ kāmaye priyam ||
english: The charm that makes the ruddy sheldrake one's own — this captivating charm. May it make that dear one my own, the one whom I love.

sanskrit: yat kakṣīvāṃ saṃvananaṃ cyavanaś cakra āsuraḥ | tad vāṃ kṛṇomi dampatī saṃ priyau bhavataṃ yuvam ||
english: The love-charm that Kakṣīvān worked, that the mighty Cyavana performed — that I work upon you two, husband and wife; may you two be united and dear to each other.

sanskrit: yathā saṃyuktau pakṣiṇau saṃpriyau carato mṛgau | evā saṃyuktau brahmaṇā saṃpriyau bhavataṃ yuvam ||
english: As two birds joined together, as two deer who roam in mutual love — so joined by sacred power, be mutually beloved, you two.

sanskrit: prehi pra hara pādāv ā gṛhebhyaḥ svastaye | kapiñjala pradakṣiṇaṃ śatapatrābhi no vada ||
english: Go forward, stride forward with your feet to the houses for well-being. O partridge, circle to the right and speak to us with the śatapatra bird.

sanskrit: bhadraṃ vada dakṣiṇato bhadram uttarato vada | bhadraṃ purastān no vada bhadraṃ paścāt kapiñjala ||
english: Speak auspiciously from the south, speak auspiciously from the north. Speak auspiciously to us from the east, O partridge, speak auspiciously from the west.

sanskrit: śunaṃ vada dakṣiṇataḥ śunam uttarato vada | śunaṃ purastān no vada śunaṃ paścāt kapiñjala ||
english: Speak prosperity from the south, speak prosperity from the north. Speak prosperity to us from the east, O partridge, speak prosperity from the west.

sanskrit: yauvanāni mahayasi jigyuṣām iva dundubhiḥ | kapiñjala pradakṣiṇaṃ śatapatrābhi no vada ||
english: You magnify youthful powers like a war-drum of the victorious. O partridge, circle to the right and speak to us with the śatapatra bird.

sanskrit: ut tabhnāmi gavāṃ kṣīram ud rathaṃ rathavāhanam | ut tabdhā asmākaṃ vīrā mayi gāvaś ca gopatau ||
english: I prop up the milk of the cows, I prop up the chariot and its draught-animal. May our heroes stand propped up, and the cows rest in me, in the lord of cattle.

sanskrit: ut tvā stabhnātu savitā devo agnir un mitrāvaruṇāv aśvinobhā | sarvān sapatnān avadhīr yugena viśāṃ patir upasattaidhy atra ||
english: May Savitṛ prop you up, may the god Agni, may both Mitra-Varuṇa, may both Aśvins. You have slain all rivals with the yoke. O lord of the clans, come and seat yourself here.

sanskrit: tvaṃ hi rudra vaśinī nirniṣe tvaṃ deveṣūta mānuṣeṣu | yad īśāno nayasi yac ca haṃsy asmākam astu pitṛṣu svadhāvat ||
english: You, O Rudra, are the ruling goddess who grants fulfillment — you among gods and also among humans. What you as sovereign lead forth, and what you slay — may that be with our fathers, rich in offerings.

sanskrit: vāyav ā rundhi no mṛgān asmabhyaṃ mṛgayadbhyaḥ | sa no nediṣṭham ā kṛdhi vāto hi raśanākṛtaḥ ||
english: O Vāyu, drive the wild game toward us, toward us who are hunting. Bring them nearest to us, for the wind is made as a leash.

sanskrit: ud asurya ud u yakṛt sthāma gacchatu te punaḥ | yato nilayate yakṛt tat prastambham ājatu | memaṃ pṛthupravartane jaghanastambhinaṃ karaḥ ||
english: Let the bile rise up, let the liver rise up — may your proper station return again. From where the liver settles, let it be propped up there. Do not make this one who has wide rolling movements a stuffer of the haunches.

sanskrit: yā pārśve saṃtanoti hṛdayaṃ jihvayā saha | tāṃ tvaṃ devi pṛthivi hikkām arasāṃ kṛdhi ||
english: That which stretches the side together with the heart and tongue — that hiccup, O goddess Earth, make powerless.

sanskrit: anusṛptām ity ekā ||
english: "Crept along" — this is one verse.

sanskrit: pra patāta iti dve ||
english: "Fly forth" — these are two verses.

sanskrit: aharahar balim itye haranto 'śvāyeva tiṣṭhate ghāsam agne | rāyaṣpoṣeṇa sam iṣā madanto 'gne mā te prativeśā riṣāma ||
english: Bringing tribute day after day, O Agni, we stand like those offering fodder to a horse. Rejoicing together with wealth and nourishment, O Agni, may we, your neighbors, suffer no harm.
